## Self-review (Phase 3)

Mechanical:

- The live-only test caught a real fail-closed subtlety: clearing
  `acquisition` alone leaves `capture_method=fixture_transcription`,
  which correctly still derives non-live — the label derives from the
  record's markers, not the derived field. The test now clears every
  marker and asserts `posture.has === false`.
- `derivedAcquisition` precedence in both layers: explicit
  `acquisition` field → transcription markers → `stand-in`/`fixture`
  capture_kind → else `live_capture` only with a retrieval stamp —
  never inferred from `source_url`.
- Print footers: `class='page'` count == `class='footer'` count
  asserted (≥4 pages), each footer scanned for licence, permalink and
  the as-of pair — a per-page footer, not a document footer.
- SUPERSEDES.json digests computed over the post-generation bytes;
  CORRECTION.md edits are append-only sections; the 10-04 artifact
  sets are untouched (their recorded digests remain true).

Design:

- The disclosure's "which facts" duty (F-16) is answered at two levels:
  the JSON's `evidence_posture.stand_in_facts` names them verbatim, and
  every rendered assertion row carries its own label — a reader sees
  exactly which facts rest on stand-ins without a separate list.
- `review_label` is a closed mapping on the recorded `review_status`;
  no template branches on anything else. The print and the page both
  surface the recorded status verbatim alongside the label
  (`(recorded status not_run)`), so the derivation is auditable.
- The web guard lives in `getResearchDossierPortfolio()` — every render
  path (page, JSON endpoint, index) loads through it; a planted future
  stamp cannot reach markup.
